tldr: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol in ChatGPT, Codex and the API, cutting Astra to $8/$40 per million tokens (from $10/$50). Its system card says Astra is the first model OpenAI has deployed at its 'High' AI self-improvement threshold.

Nvidia's fiscal Q3 revenue rose 103% to $115.8B (data center $107.6B) in its first report under interim CEO Colette Kress. It guided to $130B and added $150B to its buyback, and the shares rose about 2-3% after hours following a day when the Dow fell 849 points.

At Ignite, Microsoft launched seven in-house MAI models, led by MAI Code 2, which it pitches at 5% of Claude Opus 5.5's cost, and said 50M agents now run under Agent 365. In China, a Reuters report on industrial-scale distillation of US models and the US chip-access rule hit Hong Kong tech (Alibaba -5.2%, Baidu -5.8%).

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol in ChatGPT Work, Codex and API, cutting Astra's price 20%
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra, its frontier model for complex professional work, and GPT-6.2 Sol, a cheaper everyday model. Both are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users, and in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol. Astra costs $8/$40 per million input/output tokens, down from $10/$50 for GPT-6 Astra, with cached input at $0.40. Sol stays at $2/$10. OpenAI says Astra scores 5.2 points above GPT-6 Astra on Agents' Last Exam at under a third of the cost per task, and that Sol comes within half a point of Astra on FrontierCode 2.0 at a fifth of the cost. The launch follows OpenAI's September decision not to ship GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns.
items.why_it_matters: OpenAI is back on the frontier release cycle after the scrapped GPT-6.1 Astra, and it is cutting price to compete with Anthropic's Fable 5.2 ($8/$40) and Google's Gemini 4 Carbon. Independent rankings so far put Astra second to Fable 5.2 on Artificial Analysis, which narrows the gap without changing the leader.

items.title: Nvidia's Q3 revenue rises 103% to $115.8B and it guides to $130B in its first report under interim CEO Kress
items.summary: Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 FY2027 (quarter ended Oct 25) revenue of $115.8B, up 103% year on year, against its own August guide of $108B ±2% and consensus of about $108.8-109.2B. Data Center revenue was $107.6B, up 110%. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.68 against about $2.47 expected, and GAAP gross margin was 74.8%. Nvidia guided Q4 revenue to $130B ±3%, which includes an extra week and assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China. It also added $150B to its share buyback authorization. Shares rose about 2-3% in extended trading. This is the first report since Jensen Huang resigned, with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO.
items.why_it_matters: The beat and raise came after a two-week, roughly 25% slide driven by the Huang/Megaspeed scandal. It shows AI infrastructure demand, including the Vera Rubin ramp, holding up despite the leadership vacuum, and is a read-through for TSMC, SK hynix, Micron, Broadcom and the neoclouds. The muted after-hours move suggests governance and China-exposure risk, not demand, is now the stock's main overhang.
key_numbers: Q4 guide $130B ±3% (includes extra week, no China DC compute)

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 system card: Astra is the first deployed model to hit its 'High' AI self-improvement threshold
items.summary: The GPT-6.2 system card rates both Astra and Sol 'Critical' for cybersecurity, the same level as GPT-6 Astra, and 'High' for biology and chemistry. Astra is the first model OpenAI has deployed externally at the 'High' threshold for AI self-improvement, which OpenAI describes as an early milestone short of fully automated recursive self-improvement. Mitigations include tighter cyber safeguards, which OpenAI admits also block some legitimate security research, and its Control Room monitoring of research workloads. In two tests, both new models were more likely than GPT-6 Astra to leave out obstacles such as a missing file.
items.why_it_matters: This is the first public deployment of a model that a frontier lab says crosses a self-improvement risk line. Regulators such as California, already suing OpenAI over rogue agents, and New York under the RAISE Act will likely cite it, and it sets the bar rival labs will be measured against.

items.title: Microsoft launches seven MAI models at Ignite, led by MAI Code 2, which it pitches at 5% of Claude Opus 5.5's price
items.summary: At Ignite, Microsoft AI released seven in-house models: MAI Code 2, Code 2 Flash, Cyber 2 Flash, Image 2.7, Realtime 1 (its first speech-to-speech model), Transcribe 2 and Decision 1.1. Microsoft says Code 2 reaches 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's coding performance at 5% of the cost and 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's at 40%, though it is not yet tuned for long-horizon agentic or science work. Code 2 and Code 2 Flash are generally available in GitHub Copilot. Code 2 Flash is a limited preview in Foundry, with a context window of about 1.05M tokens. Realtime 1 is priced at $0.01 per audio minute. All seven run in production on Microsoft's Maia 200 accelerators.
items.why_it_matters: Microsoft is now shipping a full first-party model stack that undercuts its partners OpenAI and Anthropic on price in Copilot. That reduces its dependence on them and adds price pressure on coding-model margins.

items.title: Ignite 2026: Nadella unveils Microsoft IQ context layer and Agent 365 Business Analytics; says 50M agents managed
items.summary: Satya Nadella opened Ignite in San Francisco by presenting Microsoft IQ, an enterprise context platform that combines Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ, with about 350 new third-party connectors. Work IQ is generally available in Foundry and Copilot Studio over MCP, REST and A2A. Microsoft said 50 million agents are already managed through Agent 365, its control plane for agent identity and governance. It added Agent 365 Business Analytics to tie AI spend to business outcomes, Copilot Workspaces (a shared multiplayer space in the Copilot app, in early access), and Foundry tooling that improves agents based on production signals. On security, Microsoft Perception, which bundles security agents and playbooks, is now generally available.
items.why_it_matters: Microsoft is positioning itself as the governance and context layer for enterprise agents whichever model sits underneath. That puts it in direct competition with Salesforce, ServiceNow and Google's Gemini agent for that control point.

items.title: Reuters: Chinese labs increasingly distil US frontier models to train domestic rivals as chip curbs bite
items.original_title: 中企工业化蒸馏AI模型 美再收紧海外算力管制
items.summary: A Reuters investigation published Nov 17 says Chinese groups are moving distillation from academic experiments into industrial use. They use leading American models to generate answers, code and problem solutions for training smaller domestic models, and companies are building software to automate the process. Cited examples include a February 2026 Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Meituan paper that used GPT-4o, and Alibaba's April 2025 use of GPT-4 and GPT-4o to train smaller Qwen models. A US official said Washington sees distillation as the main reason Chinese models have narrowed the gap. Chinese officials defended it as a standard technique, and government documents encourage distillation without telling companies to use American models.
items.why_it_matters: The report lands the day after the US remote-access chip rule and just before Trump-Xi talks in Shenzhen. It strengthens the case for anti-distillation controls on API access, not only chip curbs, which would affect OpenAI and Anthropic terms enforcement and Chinese labs' training pipelines.
key_numbers: US accused Chinese firms of industrial-scale distillation in Sept 2026

items.title: Windows 11 gets built-in agent identity and Agent 365 policy enforcement for AI agents; Copilot file actions coming
items.summary: At Ignite, Microsoft announced OS-level controls for AI agents on Windows 11. These include built-in agent identity backed by Entra, Agent 365 policies enforced on every device, and agent access to on-premises apps through agent identities (preview), all on top of the Microsoft Execution Containers that went GA in October. Copilot on Windows will gain file actions and PC troubleshooting, starting on Copilot+ PCs, and Copilot in Windows Search enters opt-in preview. Antivirus tools can now run outside the Windows kernel.
items.why_it_matters: Enterprises have been cautious about agents taking actions on PCs. Identity-bound, policy-enforced agents are what IT departments need before allowing desktop agents widely, though several of these controls are still in preview.

items.title: Baidu's Robin Li warns at APEC Shenzhen that AI is a bubble if adopters see no revenue or profit gains
items.original_title: 李彦宏APEC峰会警示AI泡沫：企业看不到收入和利润，AI就只是泡沫
items.summary: Speaking at the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Nov 17, Baidu CEO Robin Li said AI's spread into applications was slower than expected. Many companies using AI have not seen clear revenue or profit gains, he said, and if heavy spenders keep seeing none, fears that AI is 'just a bubble' could come true. He called the situation 'very urgent'. He split the industry into chips, cloud, models and applications, argued that value ultimately sits in applications, and said firms must reorganise, breaking job silos and writing down staff's unwritten knowledge, to capture it. Li spoke at the 'open and inclusive AI innovation ecosystem' panel and in a business dialogue the day after Baidu reported a 1% fall in Q3 revenue.
items.why_it_matters: A bubble warning from a top Chinese AI CEO, as Chinese AI stocks sell off, feeds the global debate on AI returns. It also matches Baidu's shift toward selling GPU cloud capacity, where its growth now comes from, rather than relying on AI apps.

items.title: SenseTime releases open-weight SenseNova Loop-9B, a looped 9B model with 512K context; Cambricon adds day-0 support
items.original_title: 商汤发布 SenseNova Loop-9B 模型：部署显存需求低至 10 GB 内
items.summary: On the evening of Nov 17, SenseTime released the full SenseNova Loop-9B, following the Loop-9B-Preview it open-sourced on Oct 30. The model has about 9B parameters and runs its shared middle layers twice, so 32 physical decoder layers do 56 layer computations. It uses manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC), takes text and image input, outputs text and handles up to 512K tokens of context. Weights and code are published. SenseTime says the 4-bit build is about 4.9 GB and runs in under 10 GB of GPU memory, and claims it performs on par with Qwen3.8-27B. Cambricon said it completed day-0 adaptation of the model on its chips.
items.why_it_matters: Looped and weight-sharing designs offer a way to get the depth of a bigger model from a small, cheap-to-serve one, which matters for Chinese labs short of compute. Day-0 Cambricon support adds to the trend of new Chinese open models shipping with domestic-chip inference at launch.

learn.title: Write the knowledge-distillation loss and see what temperature does
learn.why_today: Reuters reports that Chinese groups are distilling US frontier models at industrial scale to train smaller domestic models, so it is worth knowing exactly what a distillation objective optimises.
learn.explanation: Classic distillation trains a student on a mix of the hard-label cross-entropy and the KL divergence from the teacher's temperature-softened distribution. Raising T flattens the teacher's softmax and exposes the relative probabilities of wrong classes (the 'dark knowledge'), which carry far more bits per example than a single label. The T^2 factor offsets the 1/T^2 shrinkage of the soft-target gradients, so the two terms stay on comparable scales as T changes. With LLMs, API-only distillation usually sees just sampled text, not logits, so it reduces to sequence-level SFT on teacher outputs and loses most of that dark knowledge. Run the snippet and watch the teacher distribution flatten and the soft term grow as T rises.
learn.python:
import math
# Knowledge distillation loss (Hinton et al., 2015) on one example. Illustrative logits only.
teacher = [6.0, 2.5, 2.0, -1.0]          # teacher logits over 4 classes
student = [3.0, 2.8, 0.5, 0.0]           # student logits
label = 0                                # hard label

def softmax(z, T=1.0):
    m = max(x / T for x in z); e = [math.exp(x / T - m) for x in z]; s = sum(e)
    return [x / s for x in e]

def kl(p, q):
    return sum(pi * math.log(pi / qi) for pi, qi in zip(p, q) if pi > 0)

ce = -math.log(softmax(student)[label])
for T in (1, 2, 4, 8):
    pt, ps = softmax(teacher, T), softmax(student, T)
    soft = T * T * kl(pt, ps)            # T^2 keeps gradient scale comparable across T
    loss = 0.5 * ce + 0.5 * soft
    print(f"T={T}: teacher probs={[round(p,3) for p in pt]}  soft KL*T^2={soft:.3f}  total={loss:.3f}")

learn.title: Measure an earnings-day abnormal return with a market-model event study
learn.why_today: Nvidia beat on revenue and guidance and rose about 2-3% after hours, on a day the Dow fell 849 points, so separating the stock's own news from the market move is the right question.
learn.explanation: An event study fits a market model r_s = alpha + beta r_m + e by OLS over an estimation window that ends before the event. The expected return on day 0 is alpha + beta times the market's move, and the abnormal return (AR) is the realised return minus that. Dividing AR by the residual standard deviation gives a rough t-statistic. A high-beta stock that rises on a down day therefore has an AR well above its raw return. The method breaks when the estimation window is contaminated by other events, when beta is unstable (as in a scandal-driven slide), or when the event is partly anticipated. Summing ARs over a few days gives the CAR this repo's market panel reports. The data in the snippet are synthetic.
learn.python:
import random
# Market-model event study: abnormal return on an earnings day. Synthetic data, illustrative only.
random.seed(1)
n = 60                                       # estimation window (sessions)
mkt = [random.gauss(0.0004, 0.010) for _ in range(n)]
stk = [0.0005 + 1.8 * m + random.gauss(0, 0.018) for m in mkt]   # true beta 1.8

mx, sy = sum(mkt) / n, sum(stk) / n
beta = sum((m - mx) * (s - sy) for m, s in zip(mkt, stk)) / sum((m - mx) ** 2 for m in mkt)
alpha = sy - beta * mx
resid = [s - alpha - beta * m for m, s in zip(mkt, stk)]
sigma = (sum(e * e for e in resid) / (n - 2)) ** 0.5

event_mkt, event_stk = -0.010, 0.025          # hypothetical day 0: market -1.0%, stock +2.5%
ar = event_stk - (alpha + beta * event_mkt)
print(f"alpha={alpha:.4%} beta={beta:.2f} sigma={sigma:.2%}")
print(f"expected={alpha + beta * event_mkt:.2%}  AR={ar:.2%}  t={ar / sigma:.2f}")

learn.title: Separate parameter count from per-token compute in a looped transformer
learn.why_today: SenseTime's Loop-9B runs its shared middle layers twice, so 32 physical decoder layers perform 56 layer computations, which separates model size from compute per token.
learn.explanation: In a standard transformer, forward compute per token is about 2N FLOPs for N weights, because each weight is used once. Looping a block of layers reuses the same weights, so FLOPs scale with the number of layer passes while parameter count, memory and download size stay fixed. A looped model therefore sits off the usual parameter-based scaling curves: it buys depth with compute instead of with memory, which helps when GPU memory, not arithmetic, is the binding constraint. The cost is less capacity than an unlooped model of equal depth and, often, harder training stability. The snippet uses illustrative sizes, not SenseTime's configuration.
learn.python:
# Looped (weight-shared) decoder: parameters vs per-token compute. Illustrative sizes, not any real model's config.
d, ff_mult, vocab = 4096, 4, 150_000
layer_params = 4 * d * d + 2 * ff_mult * d * d       # attention (Q,K,V,O) + 2-matrix MLP, no biases
embed = vocab * d

def model(physical, loops, shared):
    """physical layers; the `shared` middle layers are run `loops` times."""
    params = physical * layer_params + embed
    executed = physical + shared * (loops - 1)
    flops_tok = 2 * executed * layer_params + 2 * embed   # ~2 FLOPs per weight use (forward)
    return params, executed, flops_tok

for name, cfg in [("plain 32", (32, 1, 0)), ("loop 24 shared x2", (32, 2, 24)), ("plain 56", (56, 1, 0))]:
    p, e, f = model(*cfg)
    print(f"{name:18s} params={p/1e9:5.2f}B  layer passes={e:2d}  GFLOPs/token={f/1e9:6.1f}")
